_doc.profile_specs: physical / native-format fields applied to the parametric profiles built from Tools/data/profiles. native_sensor_mm = sensor the grids were shot on; image_circle_mm = data-sheet coverage (hard black beyond it); pupil_visible_at_image_circle = fraction of the entrance pupil still unclipped at the image-circle edge wide open (sets the effective barrel length; 0.5 = one stop of corner falloff, typical for S35 primes)
_doc.projection_profiles: ideal fisheye lenses from their projection maths and data sheets (no measured grid needed)
_doc.presets: looks: profile + amount/breathing/out_of_range/wide_boost + image_circle + vignette (Physical: cos^4 + barrel clipping; Manual: curves) + bokeh (Physical: blades/barrel from specs; Manual). Petzval swirl is always manual (0 for modern primes).
_doc.note: imported by Content/Python/dynamiclens_tools.import_all(); every non-data-sheet number is flagged 'assumed' in its source string

AD_ARRI_Master.label: ARRI / Zeiss Master Prime (spherical, T1.3)
AD_ARRI_Master.source: Distortion: Andy Davis (Imagery for Media) Lens Files, grids shot on ALEXA SXT 2.8K (12-35 mm) and ALEXA Mini Open Gate (40-150 mm), solved in 3DE. Data sheet: 114 mm front, T1.3, 9-blade iris. Image circle 33.6 mm = the Mini Open Gate diagonal the grids cover (ARRI lists Master Primes as Super 35). Pupil visibility 0.5 at the circle edge: assumed (one stop corner falloff wide open). Blade curvature 0.3: assumed (ARRI describes the Master Prime iris as giving round bokeh).

AD_ZEISS_Supreme.label: Zeiss Supreme Prime (spherical, T1.5, full frame)
AD_ZEISS_Supreme.source: Distortion: Andy Davis (Imagery for Media) Lens Files, grids shot on ALEXA LF Open Gate, solved in 3DE. Data sheet: 95 mm front, T1.5, image circle 46.3 mm. Blade count 16 from Andy Davis's camera preset ini (Zeiss quotes a rounded iris). Pupil visibility 0.5: assumed. Blade curvature 0.5: Zeiss quotes a rounded iris (assumed amount).

L_Nikkor_6mm_Fisheye.label: Nikon Fisheye-Nikkor 6mm f/2.8 (220° circular)
L_Nikkor_6mm_Fisheye.source: Nikon data sheet: 220° angle of view, 23 mm image circle on 35 mm, 236 mm front diameter, f/2.8. Equidistant projection (Nikon fisheye family). Reported as the 6mm fisheye of The Favourite (Robbie Ryan, 35 mm 3-perf, Nikkor + Panavision PVintage). Unreal can render ~80° off-axis, so the outer ring of the circle is black. Blades and pupil visibility: assumed. Format: The Favourite was shot on a Panavision Millennium XL2, 35 mm 4-perf, released 1.85:1 (Kodak / Cinematography World interviews), so the native gate is the 1.85 extraction of Super 35: 24.89 x 13.45 mm.

L_Nikkor_8mm_Fisheye.label: Nikon Fisheye-Nikkor 8mm f/2.8 (180° circular)
L_Nikkor_8mm_Fisheye.source: Nikon data sheet: 180° circular fisheye, 23 mm image circle, f/2.8, 123 mm front. Equidistant projection. An 8mm fisheye is reported for Poor Things' lab scenes. Blades and pupil visibility: assumed. Format: Poor Things was shot on ARRICAM LT/ST, 35 mm 4-perf, 1.66:1 (Cinematography World), so the native gate is the 1.66 extraction of Super 35: 24.89 x 15.0 mm.

L_Nikkor_OP_10mm_Fisheye.label: Nikon OP Fisheye-Nikkor 10mm f/5.6 (180° orthographic, 20 mm circle)
L_Nikkor_OP_10mm_Fisheye.source: Nikon data sheet: orthographic projection r = f sin(theta), 180°, f/5.6. Image circle = 2f = 20 mm (circular fisheye on 35 mm). Blades, front diameter and pupil visibility: assumed. Format: The Favourite was shot on a Panavision Millennium XL2, 35 mm 4-perf, released 1.85:1 (Kodak / Cinematography World interviews), so the native gate is the 1.85 extraction of Super 35: 24.89 x 13.45 mm.

L_Optex_4mm_S16_Fisheye.label: OpTex 4mm T2 fisheye for Super 16 (Poor Things porthole)
L_Optex_4mm_S16_Fisheye.source: Robbie Ryan (Poor Things): a PL-mount OpTex 4mm fisheye made for 16mm/S16 (opens to T2) mounted on a 35mm ARRICAM, giving the vignetted 'porthole' frame. Image circle 14.5 mm = Super 16 coverage, so on a 24.9 x 18.7 mm frame most of the picture is black. Projection assumed equidistant. Front diameter, blades and pupil visibility: assumed. Native sensor set to the 35 mm frame it was used on (not the S16 gate it was designed for), so Match Camera To Profile gives the porthole. Format: Poor Things was shot on ARRICAM LT/ST, 35 mm 4-perf, 1.66:1 (Cinematography World), so the native gate is the 1.66 extraction of Super 35: 24.89 x 15.0 mm.

L_Stereographic_10mm_FullFrame.label: Full-frame stereographic 10mm (The Favourite '10mm' reconstruction)
L_Stereographic_10mm_FullFrame.source: Reconstruction. Robbie Ryan shot most of The Favourite on 'an extremely wide 10mm' (Nikkor + Panavision PVintage sets, 35 mm 3-perf); the exact lens is not named. The frames show ~130° across the diagonal with strongly bowed lines, which a stereographic projection r = 2f tan(theta/2) reproduces (corner of a 24.9 x 18.7 frame = 137° diagonal). Everything else assumed. Format: The Favourite was shot on a Panavision Millennium XL2, 35 mm 4-perf, released 1.85:1 (Kodak / Cinematography World interviews), so the native gate is the 1.85 extraction of Super 35: 24.89 x 13.45 mm.

L_Nikkor_6mm_Fisheye_Frame.label: Nikon Fisheye-Nikkor 6mm f/2.8 as framed in The Favourite (1.85:1, DI blow-up)
L_Nikkor_6mm_Fisheye_Frame.source: Nikon data sheet: 220° angle of view, 23 mm image circle on 35 mm, 236 mm front diameter, f/2.8. Equidistant projection (Nikon fisheye family). Reported as the 6mm fisheye of The Favourite (Robbie Ryan, 35 mm 3-perf, Nikkor + Panavision PVintage). Unreal can render ~80° off-axis, so the outer ring of the circle is black. Blades and pupil visibility: assumed. FRAME VARIANT: the film's fisheye frames are full-frame with only the corners rolling off. A 6 mm equidistant image reaches the corner of a 1.85:1 gate only if the corner is at most ~78 deg off-axis (the most a rectilinear Unreal render can source at overscan 2): half-diagonal <= 6 mm x 1.36 rad = 8.2 mm -> gate 14.4 x 7.78 mm, i.e. the 35 mm scan blown up ~1.7x. The real DI blow-up is unknown (assumed); the framing is what matters. Use Match Camera To Profile and Fixed overscan 2.0 on the component.

L_Nikkor_8mm_Fisheye_Frame.label: Nikon Fisheye-Nikkor 8mm f/2.8 as framed in Poor Things (1.66:1, DI blow-up)
L_Nikkor_8mm_Fisheye_Frame.source: Nikon data sheet: 180° circular fisheye, 23 mm image circle, f/2.8, 123 mm front. Equidistant projection. An 8mm fisheye is reported for Poor Things' lab scenes. Blades and pupil visibility: assumed. Format: Poor Things was shot on ARRICAM LT/ST, 35 mm 4-perf, 1.66:1 (Cinematography World), so the native gate is the 1.66 extraction of Super 35: 24.89 x 15.0 mm. FRAME VARIANT: Poor Things' 8 mm shots (ballroom, lab - Noam Kroll's article stills) fill the 1.66 frame with the corners rolling off, which a 23 mm circle on the 4-perf gate cannot do; modelled as the largest 1.66 gate whose corners stay within 78 deg off-axis (renderable at overscan 2): half-diagonal 8 mm x 1.36 = 10.9 mm -> 18.7 x 11.27 mm, a 1.33x blow-up (assumed). Match Camera To Profile.

AD_Master.label: ARRI/Zeiss Master Prime, as measured. Physical vignette and cat's eye, no swirl.

AD_Supreme.label: Zeiss Supreme Prime, as measured. Physical vignette and cat's eye, no swirl.

C_MasterHeavy.label: Master Prime x1.6 with extra barrel under 24 mm and strong breathing. Extrapolates below 12 mm; corners go black past the overscan limit.

C_Subtle.label: Supreme x0.5, no breathing, light vignette, clean modern look.

C_Vintage.label: Master profile with a mild Petzval swirl, stronger cat's eye and vignette. Below 12 mm the 12 mm coefficients are applied unscaled (raw clamp), so the barrel keeps growing as you zoom out and the edge mask sweeps in - the look Dylan liked; physically the wide end is a guess.

L_Favourite_6mm.label: The Favourite fisheye: Nikkor 6mm 220° equidistant on 35 mm. Circular image, black corners, heavy natural falloff. Edge from the film's frames: no hard rim, corners roll off over ~45% of the radius, top corners darker than bottom.

L_Favourite_10mm.label: The Favourite ultra-wide: full-frame stereographic 10mm reconstruction. Whole frame covered, bowed lines, heavy corner falloff.

L_PoorThings_4mm_Porthole.label: Poor Things porthole: OpTex 4mm Super 16 fisheye on a 35 mm frame. Small circular image, everything else black. Edge measured from a 1.66:1 still: rolloff band 0.85-1.13 of the circle radius, blue rim at 1.05-1.08, circle 5% left / 3% high of frame centre.

L_PoorThings_8mm.label: Poor Things lab: Nikkor 8mm 180° circular fisheye on 35 mm. Edge: same optical rolloff family as the 4 mm (assumed slightly tighter).

L_PoorThings_Petzval_58.label: Poor Things portraits: Lomography Petzval 58 (TLS rehoused). Round Waterhouse aperture, strong swirl wide open ('a vortex'), sharp centre. Shot wide open in the film.

L_Favourite_10mm_Rect.label: The Favourite ultra-wide, rectilinear version: Master Prime profile extrapolated to 10 mm with extra barrel. Full frame, no circle, moderate overscan.

L_Favourite_6mm_Frame.label: The Favourite fisheye as framed in the film: Nikkor 6mm blown up so only the corners roll off (top darker). On the component: Match Camera To Profile, Overscan Fixed 2.0.

L_PoorThings_8mm_Frame.label: Poor Things 8 mm Oppenheimer/Nikkor as framed in the film: full 1.66 frame, 'distinct bend', corners rolling off. Match Camera To Profile.

L_PoorThings_Petzval_85.label: Poor Things portraits: Lomography Petzval 85 (TLS rehoused). Round Waterhouse aperture, swirl wide open, sharp centre.

L_PoorThings_UltraPrime_10mm.label: Poor Things wide: ARRI/Zeiss Ultra Prime 10mm T2.1, rectilinear. Distortion placeholder (Master Prime at 12 mm) until a 10 mm grid exists.

L_PoorThings_MasterZoom_16-110.label: Poor Things zoom shots: ARRI/Zeiss Master Zoom 16.5-110 T2.6 - 'virtually no distortion or breathing'. Master Prime grid scaled down; zoom freely.

L_PoorThings_Optimo_24-290.label: Poor Things long zooms: Angenieux Optimo 24-290 T2.8. Low distortion, mild breathing (Master Prime grid scaled); zoom freely.

L_PoorThings_VistaVision_LeicaR.label: Poor Things reanimation sequence: Beaumont VistaVision (8-perf) with adapted Leica APO-Summicron-R / Telyt-R 19-135 mm. Clean full-frame glass: Supreme grid at 0.6, native 36.7 x 25.5 (~VistaVision 37.7 x 25.1). Use a 1.5:1 filmback.

C_Vintage_Raw.label: Identical to DL_C_Vintage (kept from when Vintage used the rescaled clamp).

notes.image_circle_edge_measurement_2026-09-06: Poor Things 4 mm still (1400x845 crop, 1.66:1): blurred-luminance iso-contour circle fit centre (660,411) R=364 px -> offset x=-0.057 half-width, y=-0.028 half-height; radial mean luminance plateau 0.40 at 0.75-0.85 R, 50% at 1.04 R, 10% at 1.13 R; blue fraction of RGB rises 0.25 -> 0.35 at 1.05-1.075 R (blue rim). Outer black radius 1.13 R = 0.587 of half-width = 14.6 mm circle on a 24.9 mm wide gate, matching the OpTex 14.5 mm spec.

prefixes.AD: Andy Davis (Imagery for Media) measured data - either his Lens Files fitted to K coefficients (a focus stack, so they breathe) or his creative lens maps as single-focus ST maps
prefixes.T: tiedtke Real Cinema Lenses ST maps
prefixes.L: Lanthimos films (The Favourite, Poor Things) reconstructions

L_Petzval_58.label: Lomography Petzval 58 Bokeh Control (TLS rehoused) - Poor Things
L_Petzval_58.source: Lomography data: 58 mm f/1.9, Waterhouse-stop aperture (round hole, so a round iris: 16 blades fully curved), bokeh control ring levels 1-7, covers full frame; rehoused by True Lens Services for Poor Things (Kroll / Cinematography World). Distortion: the Master Prime grid at 58 mm (assumed - no Petzval grid). Front diameter and pupil visibility assumed.

L_Petzval_85.label: Lomography Petzval 85 Art Lens (TLS rehoused) - Poor Things
L_Petzval_85.source: Lomography data: 85 mm f/2.2, Waterhouse-stop aperture (round), full-frame coverage; TLS rehousing for Poor Things. Distortion: Master Prime grid at 85 mm (assumed). Front diameter and pupil visibility assumed.

L_UltraPrime_10.label: ARRI / Zeiss Ultra Prime 10mm T2.1 - Poor Things
L_UltraPrime_10.source: ARRI/Zeiss data sheet: Ultra Prime 10 mm T2.1, Super 35 coverage, 156 mm front (assumed from the dedicated filter holder). Robbie Ryan's '10mm Arri/Zeiss' on Poor Things (Kroll). Distortion: the Master Prime grid clamped at its widest measured focal (12 mm) - a placeholder until a 10 mm grid exists; blades/pupil assumed.

andy_stmap_sets._doc: Andy Davis's free 'creative lens maps' (spherical), one ST map per prime, single focus. Imported by dynamiclens_tools.import_andy_stmaps() from half-res EXRs prepared offline; the geometry (focal list, sensor, needed overscan) is measured and comes from the prepared manifest.json, while everything here is the hand-authored editorial and physical layer. image_circle_mm is NOT set here: the importer derives it from the diagonal of the gate the grid actually covers, which is a measured floor rather than a data-sheet figure. front_diameter_mm / iris_blades / blade_curvature / pupil_visible_at_image_circle are PLACEHOLDERS (same as the tiedtke import) - they are not from data sheets and should be replaced per series as real specs are found. His anamorphic sets are deliberately not imported: they are the same measurements we already ship as DL_T_*. See SOURCES.md.

_excluded.zeiss_supreme: already shipping as DLP_AD_ZEISS_Supreme, parametric with a real focus stack, which is strictly better than a single-focus ST map
_excluded.*_ana_*: all 16 anamorphic sets are numerically identical to the tiedtke maps already imported as DL_T_*
